name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,521

clue.text: Two fantasies involving twenty French hunks basically doing everything you want

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so the first fantasy wraps around what follows
basically points to the base or start of a word, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: a lie is a fantasy or untruth; this is the first of the two
vingt is French for twenty
first letter of hunks
a dream is the second fantasy

explanation.surface: A daydreamer imagines twenty French hunks catering to every wish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two fantasies' supplies two separate words, and the French number with its companion letter nests inside the first of them only.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes enjoying a life where every wish comes true, exactly as you would imagine it.

clue.text: To play by ear is better entertaining

indicators.note: to entertain is to host or hold someone, so the first word holds the second

blocks.note: to better something is to make it superior
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician claims that playing by ear beats reading notation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is better' reads as a comparison, but 'is' is the letters held inside the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing music without a written score means making it up on the spot, which is to extemporise.

clue.text: Children matter

blocks.note: first meaning: offspring, as in 'died without'
second meaning: a subject or topic under discussion

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a slogan saying that children are important; 'matter' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means offspring in legal and formal language and also a topic or point in dispute.

clue.text: Terribly upset, grim and extremely surly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly knocked out of shape, so the next words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes a person who is terribly upset, grim and very surly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely surly' looks like the outer letters of surly, but it is the definition: the superlative form.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word for bad-tempered and sulky means most bad-tempered of all.

clue.text: Rider bears unpleasant smell that camels have

indicators.note: in a down clue one part bears, or holds up, another, so the first sits below the second

blocks.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
a rider is an addition to a document, like a postscript

explanation.surface: A rider puts up with the bad smell that camels give off.
explanation.walkthrough: Rider suggests someone on a camel, but it is an addition to a letter. Hum is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Dromedaries carry one fatty hump and Bactrians two, so these are what the animals have on their backs.

clue.text: Strong pot - perhaps from Amsterdam range

blocks.note: Amsterdam is in the Netherlands, so something from there is an example of this nationality
a range is a cooking stove, which includes an oven

explanation.surface: A sturdy cooking pot, maybe a kitchen range from Amsterdam.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym is Dutch, a small in-joke.
explanation.definitionFit: This heavy lidded cast-iron cooking vessel is sturdy enough to go on a hob or inside a stove.

clue.text: Type of chemical bonds not involving outer shell

indicators.note: without its outer shell a word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: tethers are ropes or chains that tie, like bonds

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on a compound whose bonds do not involve an outer electron shell.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonds and shell sound like chemistry terms; here bonds are tethers and the shell is the word's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ether is a class of organic compound with an oxygen atom linking two carbon groups.

clue.text: Test for health food that contains mainly mince

indicators.note: contains says the first word holds the next inside it
mainly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a meal is food
to mince or dice is to chop small

explanation.surface: A health test involving food that is mostly minced meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Mince looks like a noun for meat; it is a verb meaning chop, as dice is.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical examination by a doctor to check someone's fitness, used as a noun.

clue.text: Bygone leader wearing musty uniform

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is wanted
something worn sits inside clothes, so it goes into the word that follows

blocks.note: musty air or food is stale
the first letter of bygone

explanation.surface: A former leader still wears a musty old uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Uniform looks like clothing to go with wearing; it is an adjective meaning unchanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steady and not varying is constant and consistent, which is the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Bug-like bites

blocks.note: to bug a phone is to tap it
as and like both mean similar to

explanation.surface: Bites that resemble insect bites.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish small plates of snacks served with drinks are informally called bites.

clue.text: Name Dutch hit single

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking for the title of a Dutch chart-topping single record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit single' reads as a chart record; hit is the anagram signal and single is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a partner or pair is alone, as an unpaired sock or glove would be.

clue.text: Leak needed during regressing bar session

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the first word goes inside the other
to regress is to go backwards, so this word is read from its end

blocks.note: a pub is a bar
to ooze is to leak slowly

explanation.surface: Someone needs the toilet partway through a drinking session in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar session' reads as a single phrase, but bar belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A booze-up is a British informal term for a heavy drinking bout or party.

clue.text: Round woman's in special movie

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

blocks.note: S is an abbreviation for special
a pic is an informal word for a film
her is the woman's; the 's reads as is, joining it to in

explanation.surface: A woman stars in a special film that is round.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped like a ball, globular, which is what a curved round object is.

clue.text: Be first to go after divorcee?

indicators.note: going after means following, so the first piece is placed behind the second

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse
first is abbreviated 1st, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A question of whether one should be first to go out with someone recently divorced.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of 1st is treated as the letter I, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the sense of having being, living or being real is the verb's existential meaning.

clue.text: Peace talks mostly failing to happen

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes
failing talks collapse into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Peace negotiations largely fail to get off the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur or come about is the same as an event being held or coming to pass.

clue.text: Finally realise who in Brussels said it's indefinite

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the next word, so its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: last letter of realise
qui is French for who, and French is spoken in Brussels
vocal means spoken aloud

explanation.surface: Someone in the EU's capital eventually admits a matter is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: Brussels hints at EU officials, but it only signals that French is the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambiguous or open to more than one interpretation, avoiding a clear commitment, is vague and indefinite.

clue.text: Rough peacekeepers about to get penalised

blocks.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces
re means about or concerning
to be fined is to be penalised with a monetary charge

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers behaving roughly are about to be punished.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude, unpolished or coarse material has not been processed, which is what rough means here.

clue.text: No vegan feast lacks a litre of rye, oddly

indicators.note: lacks means is without, so these letters are removed
oddly picks the letters in odd positions: first, third, fifth

blocks.note: a carnival is a festival or feast
taken as written; removed
L is the abbreviation for litre; removed
first, third and fifth letters of of rye

explanation.surface: A meat-free festival goes without a litre of rye whiskey, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one A and the L from CARNIVAL leaves CARNIV.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat-eater is the opposite of someone who avoids all animal products, so it is no vegan.

clue.text: Dean for one is creakiest when well-oiled

indicators.note: well-oiled means drunk, and a drunk word staggers into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Dean creaks badly unless he has had a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Dean, of Torvill and Dean, is a British Olympic ice-dancing champion; the dean looks like a college official.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Dean is a famous example of a figure skater, the 'for one' marking him as an instance.

clue.text: Flibbertigibbet - a person to call into question

blocks.note: a flibbertigibbet is a frivolous, mischievous person, like an imp
each means per person, as in a pound each

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained person gets called into question.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to challenge or cast doubt on someone's honesty, or formally accuse an official.

clue.text: Loves running around pinching sister

indicators.note: pinching means stealing, so the letters are lifted from inside the phrase
turning around means facing the other way, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: the end of loves and the start of running

explanation.surface: A thief who loves running about while stealing from a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: Loves looks like zeros or affection, but it only carries letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.

clue.text: Eavesdrop to try and understand without introductions

indicators.note: with no introductions the words lose their opening letters

blocks.note: a judge will hear, or try, a case
to twig is British slang for to understand

explanation.surface: Listening in to try to understand a conversation one was not introduced to.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British informal for listening secretly to others' conversations.

clue.text: Drama writer's device to capture the young

blocks.note: a play is a drama
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A playwright uses a dramatic device to grab young audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's device' looks like a literary technique; the writer is the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a portable enclosure that keeps babies and toddlers safely confined.

clue.text: Notice one at the centre queued for so long

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

blocks.note: an ad is a notice
the Roman numeral for one
the middle two letters of queued

explanation.surface: Someone notices one person in the middle of a queue that has waited so long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' is a casual farewell, not a length of time.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word for goodbye is a farewell, as is the phrase meaning see you later.

clue.text: Advance under half of ascendant Nigerian's money

indicators.note: half of keeps only one half of the word, dropping the rest
ascendant means rising, and in a down entry a rising word reads bottom to top
in a down entry under places one part below the other

blocks.note: taken as written; its second half is kept
A is an abbreviation for advance

explanation.surface: A cash advance below a rising Nigerian's money.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigerian does double duty: its last half reversed gives NAIR, and it also tells you whose money.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is the official currency unit of Nigeria, so it is that country's money.

clue.text: Format for European gig to become increasingly steamy

indicators.note: to format is to arrange into a new layout, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written

explanation.surface: Planning a European concert that is set to get hotter and sweatier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steamy' suggests passion; here it means misted up.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy windows or mirrors are misty, so more misted up is the comparative of murky with vapour.

clue.text: European government's right response to scare tactics

blocks.note: G is an abbreviation for government
R is the abbreviation for right
eek is a cry of fright

explanation.surface: A European government responds correctly to scare tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Greece's debt crisis, but each word yields only a letter or a cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Greece is a person from a country in southern Europe, so an example of a European.

clue.text: A phoney with no sex life

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: an is the form of the indefinite article before a vowel
an imitation is a fake or phoney
it is a coy old word for sex appeal or sex; removed

explanation.surface: A fake person who has no sex life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex life' looks like a phrase; life is the definition, and IT for sex is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness, vigour and spirit, as in a face full of vitality.

clue.text: Graphic expression using exclamation mark, or just italic capitals

indicators.note: capitals are the leading letters of each word, so the initials are taken

blocks.note: the initial of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Advice on how to express yourself in writing: an exclamation mark, or simply italics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' looks like upper-case typing advice; it asks for the first letter of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Small digital pictures used in texts to convey feelings are graphic expressions of mood.

clue.text: I seek handsome United fans for joint tenderness

indicators.note: to fan is to spread out, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A personal ad: looking for an attractive Manchester United supporter for tender company.
explanation.walkthrough: Fans looks like football supporters; it is a verb meaning spreads out.
explanation.definitionFit: This is bursitis of the kneecap, a painful swelling once common among servants who knelt to scrub floors.
